title: A GWAS Hit Is a Starting Point

scenes.tts: The first film treated heritability as a pattern of variation across people. If some variation tracks genotype, which DNA differences are involved? A genome-wide association study searches without choosing a candidate gene first. Its answer also belongs to that study population and setting.
scenes.caption: The first film treated heritability as a pattern of variation across people. If some variation tracks genotype, which DNA differences are involved? A genome-wide association study searches without choosing a candidate gene first. Its answer also belongs to that study population and setting.
scenes.visual: Reuse the first film's color map exactly: BLUE = measured genetic differences and tag SNPs; GREY = environment or context; GOLD = question or candidate cause; GREEN = converging functional evidence; RED = confounding or reduced portability. Carry in the first film's crowd and computed curve. BLUE allele tiles rise from people into chromosome bars while the GOLD question fills the upper frame. Label chromosome drawings 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: The first film treated heritability as a pattern of variation across people. If some variation tracks genotype, which DNA differences are involved? A genome-wide association study searches without choosing a candidate gene first. Its answer also belongs to that study population and setting.

scenes.visual: Keep the chromosome bars moving slowly. Show the title 'A GWAS Hit Is a Starting Point' for two seconds, then transform its baseline into the horizontal axis of a genome-wide plot.

scenes.tts: Each person contributes a trait value and allele counts across the genome. At every marker, the study tests whether allele dosage is associated with the trait. The skyline is a computed plot of those tests, with taller points showing stronger evidence. Each point represents a statistical test, not a gene's importance.
scenes.caption: Each person contributes a trait value and allele counts across the genome. At every marker, the study tests whether allele dosage is associated with the trait. The skyline is a computed plot of those tests, with taller points showing stronger evidence. Each point represents a statistical test, not a gene's importance.
scenes.visual: Trait cards and BLUE allele-count tiles stream from the crowd into a fixed synthetic association calculation. Plot the resulting points chromosome by chromosome and label the skyline 'simulated, computed'. Keep points rising as tests arrive; never show more than the plot, crowd, and two input cards at once.
scenes.narration: Each person contributes a trait value and allele counts across the genome. At every marker, the study tests whether allele dosage is associated with the trait. The skyline is a computed plot of those tests, with taller points showing stronger evidence. Each point represents a statistical test, not a gene's importance.

scenes.tts: Testing many markers creates many chances for false positives. A stringent genome-wide threshold controls that burden. Ancestry differences between cases and controls can also create false signals, so principal components help model population structure. A threshold controls false positives; it does not remove confounding.
scenes.caption: Testing many markers creates many chances for false positives. A stringent genome-wide threshold controls that burden. Ancestry differences between cases and controls can also create false signals, so principal components help model population structure. A threshold controls false positives; it does not remove confounding.
scenes.visual: Draw the conventional threshold as a horizontal line labelled 'P = 5 × 10^-8' on screen only. RED points caused by a schematic ancestry imbalance rise on several chromosomes. A principal-component adjustment slider lowers those synthetic confounded points but leaves a GOLD peak. Label the entire example 'simulated'.
scenes.narration: Testing many markers creates many chances for false positives. A stringent genome-wide threshold controls that burden. Ancestry differences between cases and controls can also create false signals, so principal components help model population structure. A threshold controls false positives; it does not remove confounding.

scenes.tts: A peak rarely identifies a causal base by itself. Nearby alleles can stay correlated for generations, because recombination separates them only slowly. That correlation is linkage disequilibrium. A harmless marker may rise because it tags a causal variant in the same inherited block.
scenes.caption: A peak rarely identifies a causal base by itself. Nearby alleles can stay correlated for generations, because recombination separates them only slowly. That correlation is linkage disequilibrium. A harmless marker may rise because it tags a causal variant in the same inherited block.
scenes.visual: Zoom the GOLD peak into a large chromosome ribbon made of six blocks. Several BLUE tag markers and one GOLD candidate variant ride together as the ribbon passes through many generations (show a run of generations with an ellipsis, not a family pedigree). A recombination cut separates an outer block while the central markers remain together. Label the inheritance cartoon 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: A peak rarely identifies a causal base by itself. Nearby alleles can stay correlated for generations, because recombination separates them only slowly. That correlation is linkage disequilibrium. A harmless marker may rise because it tags a causal variant in the same inherited block.

scenes.tts: The tallest marker sits beside several correlated neighbors. Must that tallest point be the causal variant?
scenes.caption: The tallest marker sits beside several correlated neighbors. Must that tallest point be the causal variant?
scenes.visual: Freeze the enlarged peak above its linked block. Pulse the tallest BLUE marker while several neighboring BLUE markers and the GOLD candidate move in synchrony. Put the GOLD question over the block without revealing an answer.
scenes.narration: The tallest marker sits beside several correlated neighbors. Must that tallest point be the causal variant?

scenes.visual: Hold the GOLD question. Let the linked markers drift together by a few pixels while the tallest marker keeps a slow pulse.

scenes.tts: No. Several variants correlated with the causal one can carry similar evidence. Fine-mapping uses the correlation pattern to rank variants and build a credible set, but that set still expresses uncertainty.
scenes.caption: No. Several variants correlated with the causal one can carry similar evidence. Fine-mapping uses the correlation pattern to rank variants and build a credible set, but that set still expresses uncertainty.
scenes.visual: Keep the tallest BLUE marker at its height and highlight that its linked neighbors stand nearly as tall, then transform the block into ranked variant cards. Keep several cards inside a GOLD brace labelled 'credible set'. Do not mark any card as proven or rejected; vary opacity to show ranking. Label values 'simulated'.
scenes.narration: No. Several variants correlated with the causal one can carry similar evidence. Fine-mapping uses the correlation pattern to rank variants and build a credible set, but that set still expresses uncertainty.

scenes.tts: Next ask which gene the variant affects in a relevant tissue. Colocalization tests whether trait and expression signals may share a variant. The target can be a neighboring gene, not the gene containing the marker.
scenes.caption: Next ask which gene the variant affects in a relevant tissue. Colocalization tests whether trait and expression signals may share a variant. The target can be a neighboring gene, not the gene containing the marker.
scenes.visual: Carry the credible-set brace into a schematic tissue panel. A GOLD variant sends curved dotted paths toward three labelled gene blocks. A GREEN expression trace rises beside a neighboring gene while the containing gene stays neutral. Label both paths 'candidate' and the panel 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Next ask which gene the variant affects in a relevant tissue. Colocalization tests whether trait and expression signals may share a variant. The target can be a neighboring gene, not the gene containing the marker.

scenes.tts: Editing then changes a candidate allele in the right cell type. If gene expression and a relevant cellular phenotype change, the causal explanation gains support. A cell result still does not prove an effect in a person.
scenes.caption: Editing then changes a candidate allele in the right cell type. If gene expression and a relevant cellular phenotype change, the causal explanation gains support. A cell result still does not prove an effect in a person.
scenes.visual: Transform the tissue panel into two matched cartoon cells labelled control and edited. Swap the GOLD allele tile in the edited cell. A GREEN gene-expression bar and GREEN cellular readout change together. Keep a dotted boundary before a grey person silhouette labelled 'not yet established'. Mark all readouts 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Editing then changes a candidate allele in the right cell type. If gene expression and a relevant cellular phenotype change, the causal explanation gains support. A cell result still does not prove an effect in a person.

scenes.tts: Association estimates can also become a polygenic score. Each allele count is weighted by its estimated effect, then the terms are summed. The score must be tested in people who were not part of the original study.
scenes.caption: Association estimates can also become a polygenic score. Each allele count is weighted by its estimated effect, then the terms are summed. The score must be tested in people who were not part of the original study.
scenes.visual: The BLUE marker cards become weighted tiles on a large balance. Allele-count tiles combine under weight labels and slide into a sum box; show no worked values. Move the completed score from a discovery crowd to a separate testing crowd across a clear divider. Label the construction 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Association estimates can also become a polygenic score. Each allele count is weighted by its estimated effect, then the terms are summed. The score must be tested in people who were not part of the original study.

scenes.tts: Carry those weights into a population with different linkage disequilibrium and allele frequencies. The same tag markers may follow causal variants less closely. Prediction can weaken even when much underlying biology is shared.
scenes.caption: Carry those weights into a population with different linkage disequilibrium and allele frequencies. The same tag markers may follow causal variants less closely. Prediction can weaken even when much underlying biology is shared.
scenes.visual: Carry the same BLUE weighted tiles into a second schematic chromosome map whose LD blocks have different boundaries. Some BLUE tags drift away from GOLD candidates. A prediction gauge contracts and turns RED at its edge, while shared GREEN gene blocks remain aligned. Label both maps 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Carry those weights into a population with different linkage disequilibrium and allele frequencies. The same tag markers may follow causal variants less closely. Prediction can weaken even when much underlying biology is shared.

scenes.tts: That matters before clinical use. Training data shape accuracy, and genetic prediction carries a history of coercion. Ask who was studied, who benefits, and who controls the data.
scenes.caption: That matters before clinical use. Training data shape accuracy, and genetic prediction carries a history of coercion. Ask who was studied, who benefits, and who controls the data.
scenes.visual: The two crowds move onto opposite sides of a large prediction tool. Unequal gauge widths remain visible. Three GOLD question cards rotate into view: 'Who was studied?', 'Who benefits?', and 'Who controls data?'. Keep the background moving subtly; label the scene 'questions for use'.
scenes.narration: That matters before clinical use. Training data shape accuracy, and genetic prediction carries a history of coercion. Ask who was studied, who benefits, and who controls the data.

scenes.tts: Association narrows the search. Functional evidence in cells strengthens the case. Establishing a cause also needs whole organisms or human genetics.
scenes.caption: Association narrows the search. Functional evidence in cells strengthens the case. Establishing a cause also needs whole organisms or human genetics.
scenes.visual: Transform the genome-wide skyline into the LD block, then the credible set, then the matched edited cells, then a grey person silhouette still behind a dotted boundary. Leave a BLUE-to-GOLD-to-GREEN path across the full frame, with each stage gently pulsing in sequence.
scenes.narration: Association narrows the search. Functional evidence in cells strengthens the case. Establishing a cause also needs whole organisms or human genetics.

scenes.visual: Clear every object. Show one centered line only: 'A GWAS peak marks an associated region, not a proven cause.'
